seoTitle: robots.txt Group Merger: Effective Rules per User-agent
metaDescription: See the rules each crawler really follows after groups with the same user-agent are merged, and why the * group does not apply on top. Free.
intro: Merges duplicate user-agent groups like a crawler does and prints the effective rule set for each named crawler.
why:
Many robots.txt files have two groups for Googlebot, or a Googlebot group plus a * group. Crawlers merge groups with the same name, and a crawler with its own group ignores the * group completely. People often expect the opposite and end up with a crawler that is blocked from less than they intended.

The tool lists the effective rules per user-agent and warns when named groups do not inherit the * rules.
howTo: Read the merged rule list for each user-agent.
Check whether named groups need the * rules copied in.

faq.q: Are the * rules added to a named group?
faq.a: No. A crawler uses the most specific group that names it and ignores the * group.
Yes, groups with the same user-agent name are combined, in any order.

faq.q: Is the user-agent name case sensitive?
Does it handle several User-agent lines in one group?
faq.a: Yes. Each name gets the same rules.
